checks.s: The redline accepts Corrigan's carve-out for information independently developed 'without reference to' Confidential Information, retaining that language in the definition of Confidential Information.
The redline rejects/deletes Corrigan's proposed carve-out for information 'generally available within the data analytics industry'.

The redline retains, intact and unaltered, the exclusion for information that 'is or becomes generally available to the public other than as a result of a disclosure by the Receiving Party or any of its Representatives in breach of this Agreement'.

The redline accepts Corrigan's expansion of the Representatives definition to include affiliates and their respective officers, directors, employees, accountants, counsel, financial advisors, and consultants.
The redline adds a sentence to the effect that 'Each party shall be responsible for any breach by its Representatives (including affiliates).'
The redline accepts Corrigan's narrowed Permitted Purpose of 'evaluating a potential acquisition by Velantis of the Data Analytics Division of Corrigan' (or substantively identical language).
The redline rejects Corrigan's 3-year confidentiality term.
The redline restores Velantis's original 2-year confidentiality term from the date of the agreement.
The redline restores the residuals clause allowing the Receiving Party to use 'residual knowledge' retained in the unaided memory of its personnel, which Corrigan had deleted.
The restored residuals clause includes a qualifier that it does not apply to trade secrets or information identified in writing as 'Highly Confidential — No Residuals'.
The redline rejects Corrigan's 'highest degree of care' standard.

The redline restores language substantially equivalent to 'reasonable care, and in no event less than the same degree of care the Receiving Party uses to protect its own confidential information of a similar nature'.
The redline rejects Corrigan's language requiring the Disclosing Party to bear all costs of seeking a protective order.
The redline provides that each party bears its own costs.
The redline provides that the Receiving Party uses commercially reasonable efforts to cooperate (or substantially equivalent language).
The redline rejects Corrigan's 5-business-day return/destruction window.
The redline restores Velantis's original 10-business-day return/destruction window.
The redline adds a carve-out for electronically archived copies retained pursuant to bona fide document-retention policies.
The redline provides that such archived copies remain subject to confidentiality obligations.
The redline rejects Corrigan's 24-month non-solicitation period.
The redline restores Velantis's original 18-month non-solicitation period.
The redline rejects and deletes Corrigan's $150,000 liquidated damages provision.
The redline includes equitable relief (injunction) as the remedy for non-solicitation breach, replacing the liquidated damages provision.
The redline rejects and deletes Corrigan's entire 12-month standstill provision, including the don't-ask-don't-waive provision.
No standstill or don't-ask-don't-waive (DADW) language remains anywhere in the redline.
The cover note states that if Corrigan insists on a standstill, Velantis is willing to discuss a narrowly tailored 6-month standstill.
The cover note's standstill fallback includes a fall-away upon any third-party bid.
The cover note's standstill fallback includes no don't-ask-don't-waive (DADW) provision.
The cover note frames the standstill fallback as a negotiating concession rather than Velantis's primary position.

The redline restores Delaware as the governing law.

The redline restores exclusive jurisdiction in the Delaware Court of Chancery (or, if unavailable, the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware).
The redline retains or includes no-obligation-to-transact language (e.g., 'Nothing herein shall obligate either party to consummate any transaction').
The redline rejects/deletes Corrigan's 'no obligation to continue discussions or negotiate in good faith' language.
The redline contains counter-language substantially equivalent to 'Nothing herein shall obligate either party to consummate any transaction.'
The redline rejects Corrigan's $500,000 bond requirement for injunctive relief.
The redline restores language providing for injunctive relief 'without bond' (or 'without the necessity of posting bond').
